definitions.title: Taylor's Formula for Two Variables
definitions.latex: f(a+h, b+k) = f(a, b) + (h f_x + k f_y) + \frac{1}{2!}(h^2 f_{xx} + 2hk f_{xy} + k^2 f_{yy}) + \cdots
definitions.statement: If f and its partial derivatives through order n+1 are continuous on an open disk centered at (a, b), then f can be approximated near (a, b) by its n-th degree Taylor polynomial with remainder term.
conditions: f has continuous partial derivatives through order n+1
definitions.explanation: Derived by restricting f to the line segment connecting (a, b) to (a+h, b+k) and applying single-variable Taylor's theorem.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Enables quadratic and higher-order polynomial approximations of multivariable surfaces.

definitions.title: Quadratic (Second-Order) Taylor Polynomial
definitions.latex: Q(x, y) = f(0, 0) + f_x x + f_y y + \frac{1}{2} f_{xx} x^2 + f_{xy} xy + \frac{1}{2} f_{yy} y^2
definitions.statement: The quadratic Taylor polynomial Q(x, y) of f about (0, 0) matches the value, gradient, and Hessian matrix of f at the origin.
definitions.explanation: The quadratic terms (1/2)(h^2 f_{xx} + 2hk f_{xy} + k^2 f_{yy}) govern surface curvature and justify the Second Derivative Test.
definitions.keyTakeaway: The Hessian quadratic form dictates local surface concavity and extrema.
